Sentence (English): Decided to replace an old Kenmore dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ As for now - Best dishwasher I have owned. ] || ---------------- || Decided to replace an old Kenmore dishwasher. When it was new it was pretty quiet and performed well, but now it was starting to have normal aging problems. I did a lot of searching and reading reviews for a new one in hopes that I could get a good one. Consumer Reports seemed to always have Bosch on or close to the top. I compared different brands and narrowed it down to Bosch and another company. Then down to Bosch. As the sweat was rolling down my forehead, I decided on Bosch. Thinking my frustration was over, I needed to decide on the model. Bosch had a new model out and I thought surely it has worked all the bugs out with this new one, but as I read and compared the reviews, this older model (Benchmark® Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N) had better reviews. People seemed to have more issues with the newer one. So, I bit the bullet (and paid the dental bill) and went with the older model. It cost more than what I was expecting to pay for a dishwasher, but my wife was the one that was going to use it the most. A happy wife is a happy life. I am 70 and did the installation myself. Once delivered, I checked it out for damage, and it was looking good. All parts were accounted for. Since my Kenmore was hard wired, I bought the optional adapter (M957-JUNCTION BOX FOR HARDWIRING - Home Depot). I also purchased the extra M939-DISHWASHER PARTS KIT & ADAPTER - Home Depot. Glad I did. I needed that right angle doohickey thing to attach the water line. I had to rearrange the plumbing a little since the water connection was in the same cabinet space and needed to be moved into the sink cabinet area. The same for the electric and optional plug adapter needed mounted. I set the dishwasher in front of the opening and the supplied water line, drain line and electric plug cable from the plug adapter were all long enough to easily attach to the dishwasher. I did not overly tighten the water line connection. Just enough to get it snug (over tightening is just as bad as not tightening enough). So, with a little prayer, I turned the water on to test it. No leaks. Still, I was concerned about a leak occurring as I was moving the unit in place since the connection is in the back of the unit. The water connection cannot be seen from underneath the outside front of the unit. By the time a leak is detected, it would be a mess. As I slowly scooched the unit under the counter, I would grab the water, electric and drain lines and pull them to take up the slack so as not to crimp them behind the dishwasher. Once in place, I secured the dishwasher to the cabinets. Just as a note, the unit came with all the correct attachment parts for different countertop scenarios, such as granite, quartz, or Formica. Connected the drain line to the garbage disposal inlet and turned the electric on. Now for the test (of course this was after reading the manual thoroughly through – yeah right). Put a few dishes in, tapped a couple of buttons and closed the door. As my wife and I looked at each other, I asked, "is it running? " She answered, "I don't know." After a few more seconds we heard a very slight hum and the timer on the front was counting down. Success! Now for a few comments. I am not sure how useful the app and internet connection to the dishwasher is. It tells you when it is done. No big deal to me. The app does provide some useful info such as manuals. Remote controlling doesn't really do much for me. When I have a load of dishes, I run the dishwasher. Since it is new, when we get a notice that it is done, we say, "that's neat". Long term, I suspect that it will be just forgotten. As far as cleaning goes, so far it seems to do a VERY good job. Definitely, noticeably better than our older dishwasher. We haven't had any tough stuff yet, so we'll have to wait for that. It is very quiet. Unless you were specially listening for it, you would just forget that it was on. A little more noise is apparent when it is draining, but still hardly noticeable. Our other dishwasher had a visible glass indicator for the Jet Dry where you could tell when to add more. We wondered how we would know on this since there was no viewer port. Interestingly there is a little red indicator that turns on when it needs refilling. I would have known this if I had really read the manual through. The only issue I have had, is that when I close the door, it kinda slams shut. My old DW had a handle that I would grab as I closed this. This doesn't. The "handle" is recessed and is a little difficult to grab as the door is swinging shut. This issue is offset by the fact that I do not have to try to clean around a handle. This is a lot easier to wipe clean. This unit has three racks. They seem to have a slight catch when fully pushed in, so they don't roll out. Important if you don't take the time to level it properly as directed – which I, thankfully, did. The top is for silverware, knives, and such. This does a better job of cleaning them rather than having silverware bunched up in a basket. The middle rack is adjustable in height. I would adjust it when there are no dishes in it. The weight can let it drop hard and might startle you. We adjusted it once and it will probably stay the way we set it most of the time. It doesn't adjust real smoothly and you have to fiddle with it a little to get it to go up or down. And lastly, while this is a no fingerprint stainless steel, it does get smudges – just not nearly as bad and is easier to clean. Hopefully it will last a long time. As of now, it is the best (and most expensive) dishwasher I have owned.

When it was new it was pretty quiet and performed well, but now it was starting to have normal aging problems. I did a lot of searching and reading reviews for a new one in hopes that I could get a good one. Consumer Reports seemed to always have Bosch on or close to the top. I compared different brands and narrowed it down to Bosch and another company. Then down to Bosch. As the sweat was rolling down my forehead, I decided on Bosch. Thinking my frustration was over, I needed to decide on the model. Bosch had a new model out and I thought surely it has worked all the bugs out with this new one, but as I read and compared the reviews, this older model (Benchmark® Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N) had better reviews. People seemed to have more issues with the newer one. So, I bit the bullet (and paid the dental bill) and went with the older model. It cost more than what I was expecting to pay for a dishwasher, but my wife was the one that was going to use it the most. A happy wife is a happy life. I am 70 and did the installation myself. Once delivered, I checked it out for damage, and it was looking good. All parts were accounted for. Since my Kenmore was hard wired, I bought the optional adapter (M957-JUNCTION BOX FOR HARDWIRING - Home Depot). I also purchased the extra M939-DISHWASHER PARTS KIT & ADAPTER - Home Depot. Glad I did. I needed that right angle doohickey thing to attach the water line. I had to rearrange the plumbing a little since the water connection was in the same cabinet space and needed to be moved into the sink cabinet area. The same for the electric and optional plug adapter needed mounted. I set the dishwasher in front of the opening and the supplied water line, drain line and electric plug cable from the plug adapter were all long enough to easily attach to the dishwasher. I did not overly tighten the water line connection. Just enough to get it snug (over tightening is just as bad as not tightening enough). So, with a little prayer, I turned the water on to test it. No leaks. Still, I was concerned about a leak occurring as I was moving the unit in place since the connection is in the back of the unit. The water connection cannot be seen from underneath the outside front of the unit. By the time a leak is detected, it would be a mess. As I slowly scooched the unit under the counter, I would grab the water, electric and drain lines and pull them to take up the slack so as not to crimp them behind the dishwasher. Once in place, I secured the dishwasher to the cabinets. Just as a note, the unit came with all the correct attachment parts for different countertop scenarios, such as granite, quartz, or Formica. Connected the drain line to the garbage disposal inlet and turned the electric on. Now for the test (of course this was after reading the manual thoroughly through – yeah right). Put a few dishes in, tapped a couple of buttons and closed the door. As my wife and I looked at each other, I asked, "is it running? " She answered, "I don't know." After a few more seconds we heard a very slight hum and the timer on the front was counting down. Success! Now for a few comments. I am not sure how useful the app and internet connection to the dishwasher is. It tells you when it is done. No big deal to me. The app does provide some useful info such as manuals. Remote controlling doesn't really do much for me. When I have a load of dishes, I run the dishwasher. Since it is new, when we get a notice that it is done, we say, "that's neat". Long term, I suspect that it will be just forgotten. As far as cleaning goes, so far it seems to do a VERY good job. Definitely, noticeably better than our older dishwasher. We haven't had any tough stuff yet, so we'll have to wait for that. It is very quiet. Unless you were specially listening for it, you would just forget that it was on. A little more noise is apparent when it is draining, but still hardly noticeable. Our other dishwasher had a visible glass indicator for the Jet Dry where you could tell when to add more. We wondered how we would know on this since there was no viewer port. Interestingly there is a little red indicator that turns on when it needs refilling. I would have known this if I had really read the manual through. The only issue I have had, is that when I close the door, it kinda slams shut. My old DW had a handle that I would grab as I closed this. This doesn't. The "handle" is recessed and is a little difficult to grab as the door is swinging shut. This issue is offset by the fact that I do not have to try to clean around a handle. This is a lot easier to wipe clean. This unit has three racks. They seem to have a slight catch when fully pushed in, so they don't roll out. Important if you don't take the time to level it properly as directed – which I, thankfully, did. The top is for silverware, knives, and such. This does a better job of cleaning them rather than having silverware bunched up in a basket. The middle rack is adjustable in height. I would adjust it when there are no dishes in it. The weight can let it drop hard and might startle you. We adjusted it once and it will probably stay the way we set it most of the time. It doesn't adjust real smoothly and you have to fiddle with it a little to get it to go up or down. And lastly, while this is a no fingerprint stainless steel, it does get smudges – just not nearly as bad and is easier to clean. Hopefully it will last a long time. As of now, it is the best (and most expensive) dishwasher I have owned.

Sentence (English): If you're on the fence about buying this it's time to make the jump and buy it now.
Comments (English): [ Best Diswasher ever made!  ] || ---------------- || If you're on the fence about buying this it's time to make the jump and buy it now. Here's my top 10 Reasons why:. #1 Steam cleans, sanitizes, and drys like champ! This hammers through impossible tasks like burnt on lasagna likely because the steam loosens it first. It also uses steam at the end to eliminate spots on glassware. Anyone reviews you read here that said this appliance \"doesn't dry\" must not be using rinse aid. Rinse aid is cheap and lasts a very long time. It notifies you when it's low. Even on 1 hour mode everything is both crystal clean and bone dry (yes even the plastics). #2 Better than the Bosch 800! It's built better, more reliable, packed with way more features, and it's $500 cheaper! The Bosch has a pop open door but this instead has a fan and a vent which does the same thing but better. I returned the Bosch 800 for this after a month because I hated that it was so boring and the tines were too close together making it hard to fit many of my dishes, pots and pans. Now I have this amazingly ungraded appliance instead. #3 Tub lights. Very bright. Awesome to see your dishes when loading and unloading. Nobody else has this and it's really nice. #3 Hidden front clock. I still don't understand where the light even comes from. You literally can't see it until it comes on. It reminds me of the heads up display hologram on car windshields. I like how you get confirmation it's on and the time left and can see when it's done. #4 The app. if you are techy the app has a ton of extra modes, remote starts, and can send notifications when finished. #5 Endless adjustability . A. Best Top 3rd rack in the game by far. The left side drops up and down to fits small cups and more low profile things like butter dishes and ramekins. The right side has a removable cutlery rack that can be used to fit all of the silverware so you can take the big trey out and have much more room. B. All the tines on the 1st and second racks flip up and down and clip in very securely. I read they go up and down to easily on accident and that is not the case. There is always a way to make all the dishes fit perfectly with the endless options. I like they are speed out wider than the Bosch and can fit thicker plates and dishes easier. The Bosch tines were so skinny I was going to have to buy all new plates to make them fit. C. Stemware racks that go up and down when need. #6 highly intelligently designed racks that slide butter smooth with the high end rollers. They have great angles that just work to fit more things comfortably. #7 1 hour mode. It is unbelievable how well it cleans. All the modes are great but if you can save money on power and use less water to be done in an hour why not always use the one hour mode? #8 Total bargain. This is essentially the same dishwasher and the $1800 signature line but this one I think is better because it has the hidden digital clock on front and no LG badging which is great because you can match it with Samsung or any other stainless steel non LG appliances. The only thing that the Signature line has that's \"better\" is 38DB as opposed to 42DB but this model is already silent. If you can't hear 42 why would you pay extra for 38? Silent is silent. I have OCD and studied all the top models from all the other brands and nobody can hold a candle to this dishwasher. I would pay $2000 for this appliance. #9 Quad wash. It has sprays below the bottom and the second rack so you know that everything is getting more clean than other dishwashers no matter what you put on the bottom level like large cups and salad bowls which would prevent water from reaching the upper levels. #10 Looks! The pocket door is very sleek and high end plus it's lower profile and much better than having a handle sticking out further in your kitchen. Top control are nice and make it perfectly minimalistic. Front controls are ugly and old school IMO. Tips: I made one small upgrade was I bought the LG silverware rack from an older model which splits into 3 separate sections for $18. I now can use the original after a dinner party or only 1 or 2 pieces for added versatility. You can fit those on the middle rack but I usually just use the top 3rd cutlery side to free up the extra room below. If you don't use a lot of silverware very often like me it's very well built but just larger than I typically need.

Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher in March 2023 after much research.
Comments (English): [ Loved it, then Hated it ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher in March 2023 after much research. It was quiet and worked well for about 7 months. Then one night we found some water on the floor. Dried it up, and all was fine for a week or so, then it leaked again. It was inconsistent, as it would only leak sporadically. We had the Lowe's installation team come out, and they found no issues with how it had been installed, so we had to contact Samsung.They eventually sent a technician out; there was a major language barrier, so it was challenging to communicate with or understand him. He placed a video call with someone else at Samsung. They were unable to come up with a reason for the leak and suggested we take pictures *if* it happened again. The next time it leaked (a couple of days later), we took photos and videos and submitted these to Samsung. They again sent a technician out, who still seemed baffled by the leak. It was finally determined that they would replace the door, and this would solve the problem. We had another wait, then the technician returned and installed the new door. From then on the unit leaked every single night. We again took video footage as proof. This has led to about 2 months of back and forth with Samsung. They told us that normally they would replace the unit, but it has been discontinued; I've since read that this leak is a common issue. They determined that they would instead issue us a refund. It's been a painful process to receive it. They've asked for various documentation repeatedly, paperwork and photos they had already received. They dragged their feet, but we finally received our refund this week.Bottom line, we will never buy a Samsung appliance again.

Sentence (English): Decided to replace an old Kenmore dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ As for now - Best dishwasher I have owned. ] || ---------------- || Decided to replace an old Kenmore dishwasher. When it was new it was pretty quiet and performed well, but now it was starting to have normal aging problems. I did a lot of searching and reading reviews for a new one in hopes that I could get a good one. Consumer Reports seemed to always have Bosch on or close to the top. I compared different brands and narrowed it down to Bosch and another company. Then down to Bosch. As the sweat was rolling down my forehead, I decided on Bosch. Thinking my frustration was over, I needed to decide on the model. Bosch had a new model out and I thought surely it has worked all the bugs out with this new one, but as I read and compared the reviews, this older model (Benchmark® Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N) had better reviews. People seemed to have more issues with the newer one. So, I bit the bullet (and paid the dental bill) and went with the older model. It cost more than what I was expecting to pay for a dishwasher, but my wife was the one that was going to use it the most. A happy wife is a happy life. I am 70 and did the installation myself. Once delivered, I checked it out for damage, and it was looking good. All parts were accounted for. Since my Kenmore was hard wired, I bought the optional adapter (M957-JUNCTION BOX FOR HARDWIRING - Home Depot). I also purchased the extra M939-DISHWASHER PARTS KIT & ADAPTER - Home Depot. Glad I did. I needed that right angle doohickey thing to attach the water line. I had to rearrange the plumbing a little since the water connection was in the same cabinet space and needed to be moved into the sink cabinet area. The same for the electric and optional plug adapter needed mounted. I set the dishwasher in front of the opening and the supplied water line, drain line and electric plug cable from the plug adapter were all long enough to easily attach to the dishwasher. I did not overly tighten the water line connection. Just enough to get it snug (over tightening is just as bad as not tightening enough). So, with a little prayer, I turned the water on to test it. No leaks. Still, I was concerned about a leak occurring as I was moving the unit in place since the connection is in the back of the unit. The water connection cannot be seen from underneath the outside front of the unit. By the time a leak is detected, it would be a mess. As I slowly scooched the unit under the counter, I would grab the water, electric and drain lines and pull them to take up the slack so as not to crimp them behind the dishwasher. Once in place, I secured the dishwasher to the cabinets. Just as a note, the unit came with all the correct attachment parts for different countertop scenarios, such as granite, quartz, or Formica. Connected the drain line to the garbage disposal inlet and turned the electric on. Now for the test (of course this was after reading the manual thoroughly through – yeah right). Put a few dishes in, tapped a couple of buttons and closed the door. As my wife and I looked at each other, I asked, “is it running? ” She answered, “I don't know.” After a few more seconds we heard a very slight hum and the timer on the front was counting down. Success! Now for a few comments. I am not sure how useful the app and internet connection to the dishwasher is. It tells you when it is done. No big deal to me. The app does provide some useful info such as manuals. Remote controlling doesn't really do much for me. When I have a load of dishes, I run the dishwasher. Since it is new, when we get a notice that it is done, we say, “that's neat”. Long term, I suspect that it will be just forgotten. As far as cleaning goes, so far it seems to do a VERY good job. Definitely, noticeably better than our older dishwasher. We haven't had any tough stuff yet, so we'll have to wait for that. It is very quiet. Unless you were specially listening for it, you would just forget that it was on. A little more noise is apparent when it is draining, but still hardly noticeable. Our other dishwasher had a visible glass indicator for the Jet Dry where you could tell when to add more. We wondered how we would know on this since there was no viewer port. Interestingly there is a little red indicator that turns on when it needs refilling. I would have known this if I had really read the manual through. The only issue I have had, is that when I close the door, it kinda slams shut. My old DW had a handle that I would grab as I closed this. This doesn't. The “handle” is recessed and is a little difficult to grab as the door is swinging shut. This issue is offset by the fact that I do not have to try to clean around a handle. This is a lot easier to wipe clean. This unit has three racks. They seem to have a slight catch when fully pushed in, so they don't roll out. Important if you don't take the time to level it properly as directed – which I, thankfully, did. The top is for silverware, knives, and such. This does a better job of cleaning them rather than having silverware bunched up in a basket. The middle rack is adjustable in height. I would adjust it when there are no dishes in it. The weight can let it drop hard and might startle you. We adjusted it once and it will probably stay the way we set it most of the time. It doesn't adjust real smoothly and you have to fiddle with it a little to get it to go up or down. And lastly, while this is a no fingerprint stainless steel, it does get smudges – just not nearly as bad and is easier to clean. Hopefully it will last a long time. As of now, it is the best (and most expensive) dishwasher I have owned.

All the tines on the 1st and second racks flip up and down and clip in very securely. I read they go up and down to easily on accident and that is not the case. Comments (English): [ Very tight in there, and the buttons beep at us! ] || ---------------- || It's shiny, and the racks slide out smoothly on bearings. Everything else we don't like. With the very deep 3rd rack (which I thought was great before I USED it), everything else is VERY tight. I can no longer put serving platters or cutting boards on the bottom rack, even when we raise the 2nd. I don't use the top for very much, and when I do it's hit or miss if it'll get cleaned, since only half of it gets water from the bottom. The buttons on top of the door are SO SENSITIVE that every time we open or close the dishwasher, it beeps at us and we have to see if it's going to try to run before we close it. That's a HUGE pain, and one we won't ever get used to. (It's been a few months already, and it's just as annoying.) We don't like using the inserts on the top of the silverware rack, but it's so wide that utensils scrape along the side of the dishwasher when we open and close it. We DO like that the tines in the 2nd rack are far enough apart to fit all coffee mugs between them, and that there's enough room for tall cups if you put them on the right side (where the 3rd rack is shallower). And again, it's shiny.

Sentence (English): After spending a week figuring out what buttons to push to get it to wash correctly, the dishwasher works well.
Comments (English): [ Complicated for us old folks ] || ---------------- || After spending a week figuring out what buttons to push to get it to wash correctly, the dishwasher works well. Gone are the days where you simply push a start button and it washes the dishes! I had to put together a simple Word document with pictures and tape it to the wall that my 78 year old wife could follow. I expect after using it a number of times, it will become second nature. My wife asked "how do we know when it's finished"? I looked through the quick start guide and didn't see the answer. I figured out that there is a red light shining below the door onto the floor and, when the light goes out, it's finished. Not very intuitive. If you have a bright kitchen, you would not easily be able to see the red light. Also, we opened the door before it was finished, then closed it again and it didn't keep going from where it stopped (left water in the bottom). I'm still unclear if we're supposed to hit the start button again or not?

My advice to anyone in the market, do your research and read read read reviews which I failed to do the first time. Sentence (English): Purchased this dishwasher August of 2020, just over 2 years later the dishwasher stopped working.
Comments (English): [ Disappointment ] || ---------------- || Purchased this dishwasher August of 2020, just over 2 years later the dishwasher stopped working. Started displaying an E:20 code (The E20 error in the Bosch dishwasher indicates problems of the circulation pump. In addition, its parts or winding might be damaged.) Went through all the troubleshooting steps, check filters, check drainline, etc., no improvement. Replaced the drain pump, still no improvement, Replaced the heat / circulation pump, still no improvement. Was finally able to locate & get a "Bosch approved" repair technician to look at the dishwasher and not really find anything wrong with the heating and circulation system, so he is speculating it must be the control board. We've been without a dishwasher for well over a year now. This whole experience with Bosch, from the product, to the ability to find and get a "Bosch qualified technician" on site, or being able to contact a Bosch tech over the phone has all been very frustrating! Previously a big fan of Bosch products, specifically tools, I assumed Bosch appliances would be of equal quality, durable & lonlasting. This has proven not to be in my case & i'll likely not consider Bosch products in the future.

Sentence (English): Everything is run by computer chips nowadays including dishwashers, and my top of the line Bosch dishwasher is no exception.
Comments (English): Everything is run by computer chips nowadays including dishwashers, and my top of the line Bosch dishwasher is no exception. Thus, there are a lot of dishwashing "options" to choose from, which can and do introduce some confusion. A good operating instruction manual can minimize confusion. Unfortunately Bosch's manual is not "intuitive," simple, or straight forward. I'm a mechanical engineer and I have yet to be able to figure out how to employ all the offered features and options due to the poor writing and presentation in the manual. Otherwise, the dishwasher appears to work as designed.

Unfortunately Bosch's manual is not "intuitive," simple, or straight forward. I'm a mechanical engineer and I have yet to be able to figure out how to employ all the offered features and options due to the poor writing and presentation in the manual. Otherwise, the dishwasher appears to work as designed.

I was just about to see if I could return it and then decided to add even more jet dry liquid than I already had. That seemed to fix the problem for now. The third rack is mostly unusable as it is far too shallow to put anything larger than flatware. I do not understand the layout of the bottom row with the splayed out prongs. Nothing fits in there except plates. Bowls roll right off. I was planning to purchase a different GE model, but the salesman in store suggested this one due to the silverware sprayers. I have noticed no difference from my prior KitchenAid dishwasher that was a work horse. Had a terrible install service as well. They tried to stick someone else's dishwasher in before I walked in and noticed it was the wrong one. They also did not protect my floors and advised they would not be doing so and then continued to scrape both of the dishwashers they brought in across my floor. They seemed inexperienced and thought my dishwasher was hardwired, which it is not.

Comments (English): [ Series 6 Bosch Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || No doubt this is a very good dishwasher. It has performed flawlessly since installation. The water solenoid is now right at the tap where the water inlet hose joins on. In most cases this will need a widening of the current 50 mm hole. How to use a level to adjust things. You need to learn how to set up the feet and adjust the two at the front and the remote one at the back. Finally there are two little grey plastic things that you have to get right to screw the dishwasher permanently to the sides. Its not mission impossible but it does take time and some figuring out. Take it slow and figure it out. Last time appliances online brought a washing machine I got it installed and lessons. I wrongly thought I was getting the same thing this time. This appliance becomes MUCH more expensive if you have to pay somebody $250 to install it. I hope you can handle 2 QR codes, pdfs, possible need to cut larger holes in your kitchen, levelling and hose and tap installations or pay the extra $250. What is REALLY needed is an unpack to fully installed video in ONE file -not lots broken up. My son is a pullapart IT guru and it took both of us to get it all right. This is a good machine BUT you dont know how good your appliance is until the day it finally dies. Hobart dishwashers did three minute fully clean cycles 40 years ago. Todays u beaut is less powerful with hour long cycles to save water and electricity. I believe all dishwashers are poorly designed (water, jets and length of cycle) as they all belong to societies with the same protocols. They COULD be much faster and much simpler with less delicate circuit boards that end up causing problems. Enjoy your bosch dishwasher

Comments (English): [ Super super super quiet! Dishes come out clean ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Pros: super quiet - main reason i bought this model. If you have a family room right next to the kitchen with an open floor plan, you will not know that the washer is running. Even standing next to the washer while running, you can barely tell that it's on. The main wash cycle seems long - with heat drying it'll run about 2.5 hours - BUT the dishes come out clean and i don't care about the length because i can run it at any time of day and night because it's so quietCons: self installation was an issue for two main reasons: 1. The diameter of the old drain hose was different than for this washer (by 1/4”) not a big difference but this required me to get a size converter in order to hook up the new drain hose to the sink drain. 2. the big issue was that the unit was delivered WITHOUT the heat element being connected (the wire connectors were loose under the washer). After the install i noticed that the washer was not drying the dishes and had to trouble shoot that issue and has to uninstall the washer and reinstall after i connected the heater element. I wish there was more configurability inside the washer like on some higher end models but i was constrained by the no1 priority of the washer being as quiet as possible so i chose this one

Sentence (English): I am happy with the purchase.
Comments (English): [ Bosch SMV6ZCX10E dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I am happy with the purchase. The dishwasher works very quietly and is intuitive to use. It washes and dries great. When I used my previous dishwasher from another company, I did not take the dishes out without using a cloth multiple times. I was skeptical about the cutlery drawer, because I thought that putting them in the basket was more efficient. However, my concerns were unfounded. Putting them on the shelf is not a problem and arranging them in individual groups makes it easier to take them out later. A big plus of the dishwasher is the function with the time display on the floor. There is no need to open the dishwasher during washing to check the time remaining until the end of the work. The dishwasher has a sufficient number of washing programs. The advantage is the possibility of shortening the program's working time, washing with half a load, controlling via the Internet or delaying the start. One small disadvantage is the fully, not partially, foldable spikes in the lower basket. I think that partially folding them out would make it easier to arrange pots and dishes in one row.
Comments (Original): [ Zmywarka Bosch SMV6ZCX10E ] || ---------------- || Jestem zadowolona z zakupu. Zmywarka pracuje bardzo cicho, jest intuicyjna w obsłudze. Super domywa i suszy. Użytkując poprzednią zmywarkę innej firmy, nie wyciągnęłam naczyń bez wielokrotnego użycia ściereczki. Byłam sceptycznie nastawiona do szuflady na sztućce, gdyż uważałam, że wkładanie ich do koszyka przebiega sprawniej. Jednak obawy były bezpodstawne. Układanie na półce nie stanowi problemu i ułożenie ich w poszczególnych grupach, ułatwia późniejsze wyciąganie. Dużym plusem zmywarki jest funkcja z wyświetlaczem czasu na podłodze. Nie ma konieczności otwierania zmywarki podczas mycia, by sprawdzić czas pozostały do końca pracy.Zmywarka ma wystarczającą ilość programów zmywania. Zaletą jest możliwość skrócenia czasu pracy programu, mycie z połową załadunku, sterowanie przez Internet czy opóźnienie startu. Jednym małym minusem są w całości, nie w części, rozkładane kolce w koszu dolnym. Uważam, że częściowe ich rozkładanie ułatwiłoby ułożenie garnków i naczyń w jednym rzędzie.

Comments (English): [ Super super super quiet! Dishes come out clean ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Pros: super quiet - main reason i bought this model. If you have a family room right next to the kitchen with an open floor plan, you will not know that the washer is running. Even standing next to the washer while running, you can barely tell that it's on. The main wash cycle seems long - with heat drying it'll run about 2.5 hours - BUT the dishes come out clean and i don't care about the length because i can run it at any time of day and night because it's so quiet. Cons: self installation was an issue for two main reasons: 1. The diameter of the old drain hose was different than for this washer (by 1/4”) not a big difference but this required me to get a size converter in order to hook up the new drain hose to the sink drain. 2. the big issue was that the unit was delivered WITHOUT the heat element being connected (the wire connectors were loose under the washer). I noticed that during my installation BUT i assumed that these were extra connectors for some functionality that my washer was not equipped with. After the install i noticed that the washer was not drying the dishes and had to trouble shoot that issue and has to uninstall the washer and reinstall after i connected the heater element. I wish there was more configurability inside the washer like on some higher end models but i was constrained by the no1 priority of the washer being as quiet as possible so i chose this one

Sentence (English): We ordered a 500 series bosch after seeing and using one, and loving it.
Comments (English): [ Bosch ruined what was an excellent dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We ordered a 500 series bosch after seeing and using one, and loving it. However, the dishwasher that was delivered was not at all what we ordered. With this update to the 500 series, bosch switched from tactile(moving, pressable) buttons to capacitive touch(hard touchscreen-style) buttons. So, be careful. every time you open or close the dishwasher, you run the risk of touching a button - and then, when you close the dishwasher havining turned it 'on' but not starting a cycle, it beeps angrily at you. In our house, the dishwasher gets opened and closed dozens of times before each load. Which means it accidentally gets turned on far more often than it gets intentionally turned on to start a cycle. So, let's say you get to the point you actually do want to start a cyle. Do you happen to be trying to set the dishwasher with wet hands? Sorry. it's not going to read your presses right. I guess they don't expect someone doing the dishes to have wet hands. Do you prefer to wash dishes with gloves on? Sorry again, these buttons aren't going to work for you. Do you happen to have chronically dry hands? Be ready for frustration when it can't sense your fingers. Do you happen to live with elderly family members who have vision difficulties? Well, i'm sure they'll love the fact that they get to be even more dependent on others when they find they can't operate the dishwasher without help. But it's ok - maybe you have kids. You could assign a kid to start the dishwasher for their grandparent. But, you better only ever use the 'normal' setting. Cause if you want to do anything fancy - like, a quick wash, rinse only, etc. - then you need to use an app. So great. you bought your kid a phone so they can use the app so they can run a quick cycle for their grandparent who can't use the buttons. But, you better have internet access. You can't set up and use your dishwasher without internet access. And part of that process, you need to make an account and login. But wait - your kid's not 18. The terms of use prohibit minors from creating an account, so they can't use the app, so they can't run a quick cycle for their grandparent who can't use the difficult touch interface themselves. So, Bosch, you used to make great dishwashers. You may still make great dishwashers, but right now your entire lineup is unusable by 2 out of the 3 generations present in many households. I truly hope you think about how bad and user-hostile these recent design decisions are and correct them in future models.

Sentence (English): This little washer was perfect for my needs.
Comments (English): [ Surprised by capability and quality. ] || ---------------- || This little washer was perfect for my needs. I spent weeks looking for a portable dishwasher once I moved into my new place. It was a pain in the rear to unbox but once I got the dishwasher into place and installed the faucet adapter I was ready to go. I hooked it up and turned on the water and was immediately soaked by a spray of water from the adapter. Whoops. Removed and reinstalled with various included washers several times. I really had to crank on the adapter to get it to handle the water pressure and the flow of water from the tap is kind of out of control now, but hey, l'm never hand washing dishes again so I don't care.With quality detergent, this dishwasher absolutely cleans the dirtiest of dishes. It can even sanitize. The run times are pretty long on higher settings and I'm betting the power consumption goes up just as much, but the standard setting is 90 minutes and cleans everything I put in it while using a shockingly small amount of water. At the end of a cycle it steams the remaining water and all you have to do is let the steam out and viola, dry-ish clean dishes.It's a bit cramped inside so I had to learn how to properly load it, same as any dishwasher. RTFM. If you just put dishes in any old way it won't clean properly. The largest pots, pans and casserole dishes don't fit as well or not at all so temper expectations and expect to still have to hand wash the largest of your kitchen cookware, though I admit to being surprised by what I have stuffed inside of this machine.The top rack also has its own washer arms so it has to mate with a water outlet in the back of the washer. If you don't check that this is properly seated then the door won't close fully and you may damage something. I haven't damaged anything yet after months of heavy use but if there is a failure point anywhere on this machine, it might be me breaking something by closing the door too enthusiastically while the top rack isn't fully seated.For apartment or trailer park living, this dishwasher is perfect. I love the counter space it adds to my kitchen by virtue of having a built-in countertop. I can wheel it around easily and don't have to hand wash dishes every day so the fact that it looks nice while it does a good job of washing them for me is just icing on the cake.Docked a star for issues with the adapter and a finicky top rack.

Sentence (English): This little washer was perfect for my needs.
Comments (English): [ Surprised by capability and quality. ] || ---------------- || This little washer was perfect for my needs. I spent weeks looking for a portable dishwasher once I moved into my new place. It was a pain in the rear to unbox but once I got the dishwasher into place and installed the faucet adapter I was ready to go. I hooked it up and turned on the water and was immediately soaked by a spray of water from the adapter. Whoops. Removed and reinstalled with various included washers several times. I really had to crank on the adapter to get it to handle the water pressure and the flow of water from the tap is kind of out of control now, but hey, l'm never hand washing dishes again so I don't care. With quality detergent, this dishwasher absolutely cleans the dirtiest of dishes. It can even sanitize. The run times are pretty long on higher settings and I'm betting the power consumption goes up just as much, but the standard setting is 90 minutes and cleans everything I put in it while using a shockingly small amount of water. At the end of a cycle it steams the remaining water and all you have to do is let the steam out and viola, dry-ish clean dishes. It's a bit cramped inside so I had to learn how to properly load it, same as any dishwasher. RTFM. If you just put dishes in any old way it won't clean properly. The largest pots, pans and casserole dishes don't fit as well or not at all so temper expectations and expect to still have to hand wash the largest of your kitchen cookware, though I admit to being surprised by what I have stuffed inside of this machine. The top rack also has its own washer arms so it has to mate with a water outlet in the back of the washer. If you don't check that this is properly seated then the door won't close fully and you may damage something. I haven't damaged anything yet after months of heavy use but if there is a failure point anywhere on this machine, it might be me breaking something by closing the door too enthusiastically while the top rack isn't fully seated. For apartment or trailer park living, this dishwasher is perfect. I love the counter space it adds to my kitchen by virtue of having a built-in countertop. I can wheel it around easily and don't have to hand wash dishes every day so the fact that it looks nice while it does a good job of washing them for me is just icing on the cake. Docked a star for issues with the adapter and a finicky top rack.

Now, I do feel the door is hard to open, not difficult, but somewhat stiff. It's most likely to avoid it from completely falling down when opening, so I can work with that. And, I would have liked a little more room at the bottom for pots and pans, but I was able to make it work. Also, the choosing cycle options was a little hard to understand, but I feel I can come to terms with that. Overall, I'm happy with how it cleans our dishes and can't wait for future uses.

First of all, I specifically asked the appliance store if there would be an issue with the old cabinet panel fitting. of course it will fit, I was assured. It did not. If the panel measurements are different, there should be a way to identify that. I had to hire a carpenter to retrofit the panel, which meant chopping part of the bottom of the cabinet off. When the washing machine is running through the cycle, it's very quiet but when it's draining the water it's extremely loud. I don't know what difference between my old vs new would cause that. Lastly, it doesn't dry the dishes. I always have the crystal dry function on and the dishwasher is always wet when the cycle is done. I just opened the dishwasher. I ran it last night. The way they designed the bottom dish rack let's you know they've never loaded one themselves. Sentence (English): This is the fourth Siemens/Bosch machine in a row.
Comments (English): [ Reliable dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This is the fourth Siemens/Bosch machine in a row. The Series 6 has lasted the longest so far, a good 8 years without service. The workmanship is top-notch and the machine is exceptionally quiet. However, this machine had a rubber/plastic smell that only disappeared after about 10 washes, which is unusual. If you're interested in app support, you can find 5 additional programs online. However, it's unclear to me why a rinsing program (cold, 15 minutes) is only available as a download. There are no programs on the machine itself that take less than 60 minutes (not even with the speed option). However, the washing performance with mixed loads of less than 60 minutes is not 100%. With mixed loads with a lot of plastic, the additional drying phase is recommended, otherwise there will be lots of drops on the dishes. The installed red rubber guard will otherwise always stay wet. The lighting is a nice touch. However, it doesn't help if you're loading the top cutlery drawer, as the many shadows are more irritating.
Comments (Original): [ Zuverlässige Spülmaschine ] || ---------------- || Dies ist die vierte Siemens/Bosch Maschine in Folge. Die Serie 6 hat bisher am längsten gehalten, gute 8 Jahre ohne Service. Die Verarbeitung ist top und die Maschine aussergewöhnlich leise.Allerdings hatte diese Maschine einen Gummi/Plastik-Geruch der erst nach ca. 10 Wäschen verschwandt, ungewöhnlich.Wer Lust auf App Support hat findet 5 zusätzliche Programme online. Allerdings ist mir unklar, warum ein Abspülprogramm (kalt, 15 Minuten) nur als Download möglich ist.Am Gerät selbst gibt es keine Programm unter 60 Minuten (auch nicht mit Speed Option). Allerdings ist die Waschleistung bei Mischbeladung unter 60 Minuten auch nicht 100%. Bei Mischbeladung mit viel Kunststoff ist die zusätzlich Trocknungsphase zu empfehlen, sonst gibt es viele Tropfen am Geschirr. Der installierte rote Gummischutz bleibt sonst auch immer nass.Die Beleuchtung ist ein nettes Kimmick. Hilft allerdings nicht wenn man die ober Besteckschulade bestückt, da irritieren die vielen Schatten eher.

Sentence (English): Dishwasher cleans exceptionally well, though cycle is a tad long, which might matter to you if trying to run multiple loads back to back.
Comments (English): [ Cleans dishes well, easily understood control ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher cleans exceptionally well, though cycle is a tad long, which might matter to you if trying to run multiple loads back to back. Not an issue in our case. The third silverware rack works well and makes loading of bottom rack easier as there need not be a silverware basket taking up space there. The washer comes with a basket, but we don't use it. Control hidden on top of door are easy enough to understand. The dishwasher is effectively silent, and when running there is a red light on shining on floor to tell you it running. Our kitchen has big frig, dedicated Iceman ice maker, drink frig, and a wine cooler, and one or more of these is running at any time. Admittedly with all the noise these make, effectively silent is a low bar for us, though you do have to put ear on door to hear it running. The washer does connect to WIFI so it can send you a notice when cycle is done and you can download custom cycles, totally useless features in my opinion. Unlike clothes washers, the install for dishwashers in not standard across different makes. Install can thus be something of a specialized chore. Our dishwasher is installed above the floor, which requires lifting it up to slide into hole (otherwise does not affect install. I purchased install and install kit mostly to get help in lift. Turns out the install was beyond the talent of installers and they gave up, leaving dishwasher in center of kitchen on floor, with random parts spread about. The install kit did not contain any parts of any use. Did get credit for install fee and install kit (which shipped back with prepaid label). Install was really pretty simple, did it myself. Admittedly made easier with washer in room, could look at connections and figure out what I needed to get from plumbing supply (or hardware) store to connect washer to house plumbing. Candidly if not up to install yourself, might be better having you local plumber do job. If your previous washer was hardwired to electricity you will also need to get electrician to install standard 120VAC/20 amp outlet. I had already done this before delivery. I did need to get help from neighbor lifting dishwasher into hole, something most would not need if installed undercounter at ground level. Washer is not particularly heavy just need two to lift it because of boxy shape. Wife appreciates the higher mount as she does not need to bend over so far to load. All in all very pleased with dishwasher, though could have had more astute install plan. Don't think this has much to do with Bosch, lack of standards across dishwashers is problem, could easily be worse with another make. See picture.

First-- I find the lower rack too easily comes off its guide rails when pushing it in or pulling it out, which requires picking it up and putting it back on the rails. Second--and this one isn't as important but I didn't realize I would miss it from my previous Monogram washer, is that there are no interior lights. I would have figured at this price point that would be an included feature. I knew going into the purchase it didn't have them, but didn't realize how much I appreciated them from our previous washer. Again, I am more than satisfied with our purchase and the model, but just a few nit picky things prevented a 5 star rating.

I want it picked up and I want my money back.

Sentence (English): After a bad experience with another brand, I chose to buy this model on sale at Lowes.
Comments (English): [ Grown to Love It ] || ---------------- || After a bad experience with another brand, I chose to buy this model on sale at Lowes. I was installing it myself and the first thing I noticed was that the inside of the dishwasher was very wet and had a very strong musty odor. I immediately called Bosch customer service and the representative was very helpful and explained that all the dishwashers were tested and would have some moisture inside. I was instructed to run the machine with a cup of vinegar and that helped with the odor, but there was still a lot of moisture at the end of the cycles. I tried several different cycles all with the same end result with clean, but still wet dishes. I contacted customer service a second time, the rep.was very helpful and asked of we wanted a service call to see if the machine was defective. They also explained the different cycles and how you can customize the cycles on the app. After downloading the app and setting the cycle I wanted with sanitizing and drying options the machine has been excellent. I am very happy with my purchase. Only thing I would improve.would be the height if the top rack. When the 3rd top rack for silverware is being used even my smaller drinking glasses do not fit on the "middle" rack. I also like that the app sends me a notification that the machine cycle has completed. Good as there is no countdown on the machine.

Sentence (English): Good dishwasher that cleans thoroughly and is easy to use.
Comments (English): [ Beautiful dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Good dishwasher that cleans thoroughly and is easy to use. The lower basket is very spacious so that even large pizza plates fit in. We only took out the upper cutlery drawer and bought a cutlery basket because we find that more convenient. Unfortunately, the control panel recently stopped responding and was no longer responsive; even after plugging and unplugging the power cord. It was no longer possible to select a program or start the machine. Only one program flashed, and after a short time everything suddenly worked again. This happened to us twice. The machine is not quite a year old and has done almost 100 wash cycles. I hope that an update via the HomeConnect app has fixed the error, because it hasn't appeared again since. Unfortunately, I haven't been able to see any further information about the update that was carried out. We'll have to wait and see. Otherwise, a decent device at a good price.
Comments (Original): [ Schöner Geschirrspüler ] || ---------------- || Guter Geschirrspüler der gründlich reinigt und leicht zu bedienen ist. Der untere Korb ist sehr geräumig so das auch große Pizzateller hineinpassen. Wir haben nur die obere Besteckschublade herausgenommen und uns einen Besteckkorb gekauft weil wir das bequemer finden.Leider hatte vor kurzem die Bedienblende Aussetzer und war nicht mehr ansprechbar; selbst nachdem der Netzstecker ein- und ausgesteckt wurde. Eine Programmwahl und das Starten war nicht mehr möglich. Es blinkte nur noch ein Programm, nach kurzer Zeit funktionierte plötzlich wieder alles. Das passierte uns 2 mal. Die Maschine ist nicht ganz ein Jahr alt und hat knapp 100 Spülgänge hinter sich. Ich hoffe das durch ein Update über die HomeConnect App der Fehler behoben wurde, denn er ist seit dem nicht wieder aufgetaucht. Leider habe ich keine weiteren Informationen zum ausgeführten Update einsehen können. Mal Abwarten. Ansonsten ein ordentliches Gerät zu einem guten Preis.
